philosophy.heading: Engineering Philosophy
philosophy.subtitle: The principles that guide how I write code.

items.title: Clean Architecture & SOLID
items.text: I separate layers with clear boundaries; on BAZR I kept a 33-entity domain model manageable this way with CQRS/MediatR.

items.title: Scalability
items.text: I don't build real-time systems bound to a single instance; on Rezervo and BAZR I designed for horizontal scaling from day one with a Redis-backed SignalR backplane.

items.title: Performance
items.text: Core Web Vitals and Lighthouse scores aren't a bonus, they're part of the deliverable — I've kept 95+ consistently across the projects I've shipped.

items.title: Accessibility
items.text: I test interfaces with keyboard navigation; aria labels and semantic HTML are a default starting point, not a layer added afterward.

items.title: Developer Experience
items.text: Type safety, a consistent folder structure, a readable commit history — that's the standard I hold myself to for code I'll reopen a year later.

items.title: Testability
items.text: xUnit/Moq on the .NET side, Jest/Supertest on Node — I don't ship critical business logic (payments, stock, authorization) to production untested.

items.title: Code Quality
items.text: FluentValidation, Zod, and Serilog structured logging — I want to catch failures in the logs before a user has to report them.

items.title: Problem Solving
items.text: I work out the data model and concurrency scenarios first; that's how TavAkademi's exam-integrity system and BAZR's stock race condition got solved.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: The most common questions about availability, working style, and technical approach.

items.question: Are you open to a full-time role?
items.answer: Yes, I'm currently open to full-time opportunities. I've been working independently/on contract since 2024 and I'm ready to move into a full-time role for the right team.

items.question: Are you flexible on remote work or relocation?
items.answer: I'm based in Turkey and fully open to remote work — I already have experience working remotely with international teams. I'm also open to discussing relocation for the right opportunity.

items.question: What's your preferred tech stack?
items.answer: I'm most comfortable with Next.js + ASP.NET Core/Node.js + PostgreSQL/MySQL, but I pick technology based on the problem — tools like CQRS/MediatR, Redis, and SignalR go in when they're needed, not because they're familiar.

items.question: How do you work within a team?
items.answer: Most of my work so far has been independent/contract, so I'm used to owning the full lifecycle from requirements to CI/CD. Clear communication, small PRs, and being open to code review matter to me.

items.question: What's your approach to testing and code quality?
items.answer: I don't ship critical business logic (payments, stock, authorization) to production untested — xUnit/Moq on the .NET side, Jest/Supertest on Node. FluentValidation/Zod for input validation and Serilog for structured logging are standard practice for me.

items.question: What's the toughest technical problem you've solved?
items.answer: On BAZR, I solved IDOR and a TOCTOU stock race condition in a payment/stock system shared across four different portals (admin/merchant/courier/customer) using RepeatableRead-isolated transactions — without a global lock.
